entries.ex: The national *curriculum* now includes coding and financial skills from primary school onwards.
entries.exAr: يتضمن *المنهج* الوطني الآن البرمجة والمهارات المالية بدءًا من المرحلة الابتدائية.

entries.exAr: يعمل كثير من الطلاب بدوام جزئي للمساعدة في دفع *الرسوم الدراسية*.

entries.ex: Adult *literacy* rates have risen sharply in many developing countries.
entries.exAr: ارتفعت معدلات *الإلمام بالقراءة والكتابة* بين البالغين ارتفاعًا حادًا في كثير من البلدان النامية.

entries.exAr: يشكو أصحاب العمل من أن بعض خريجي المدارس يفتقرون إلى *المهارات الحسابية* الأساسية.

entries.ex: Continuous *assessment* rewards steady effort rather than performance in a single exam.
entries.exAr: يكافئ *التقييم* المستمر الجهد المتواصل بدلًا من الأداء في امتحان واحد.

entries.exAr: التعليم *إلزامي* في معظم البلدان حتى سن السادسة عشرة.

entries.exAr: تؤهل الدورات *المهنية* الشباب لوظائف مثل السباكة والتمريض.

entries.ex: Most *undergraduates* in the UK complete their degree in three years.
entries.exAr: يُنهي معظم *طلاب البكالوريوس* في المملكة المتحدة دراستهم في ثلاث سنوات.

entries.ex: She is planning to do a *postgraduate* course in public health after her first degree.
entries.exAr: تخطط للالتحاق ببرنامج *للدراسات العليا* في الصحة العامة بعد حصولها على شهادتها الجامعية الأولى.

entries.ex: He won a full *scholarship* that covers his fees and living costs.
entries.exAr: فاز *بمنحة دراسية* كاملة تغطي رسومه الدراسية وتكاليف معيشته.

entries.ex: Thousands of adults *enrol* on evening classes every autumn.
entries.exAr: *يلتحق* آلاف البالغين بدروس مسائية كل خريف.

entries.ex: After she *graduated* in engineering, she found a job within two months.
entries.exAr: بعد أن *تخرّجت* في الهندسة، وجدت وظيفة في غضون شهرين.

entries.ex: Recorded *lectures* allow students to review difficult topics at home.
entries.exAr: تتيح *المحاضرات* المسجلة للطلاب مراجعة الموضوعات الصعبة في المنزل.

entries.ex: In a *seminar*, a small group discusses the week's reading with a tutor.
entries.exAr: في *حلقة النقاش*، تناقش مجموعة صغيرة قراءات الأسبوع مع المدرّس.

entries.ex: Students must submit the *assignment* online by noon on Friday.
entries.exAr: يجب على الطلاب تسليم *الواجب* عبر الإنترنت في موعد أقصاه ظهر يوم الجمعة.

entries.ex: Universities use special software to detect *plagiarism* in essays.
entries.exAr: تستخدم الجامعات برامج خاصة لكشف *السرقة الأدبية* في المقالات.

entries.ex: Regular *attendance* is closely linked to better exam results.
entries.exAr: ترتبط *المواظبة على الحضور* ارتباطًا وثيقًا بتحسن نتائج الامتحانات.

entries.ex: A teaching *qualification* is required to work in state schools.
entries.exAr: يُشترط الحصول على *مؤهل* في التدريس للعمل في المدارس الحكومية.

entries.ex: Some pupils struggle with *academic* subjects but excel in sport or art.
entries.exAr: يجد بعض التلاميذ صعوبة في المواد *الأكاديمية* لكنهم يتفوقون في الرياضة أو الفن.

entries.ex: In some schools, classes have grown to more than thirty *pupils*.
entries.exAr: في بعض المدارس، ارتفع عدد *التلاميذ* في الفصل الواحد إلى أكثر من ثلاثين.

entries.ex: Each new teacher is paired with an experienced *mentor* for the first year.
entries.exAr: يُخصَّص لكل معلم جديد *مرشد* متمرس خلال سنته الأولى.

entries.ex: Critics argue that *rote learning* produces students who can recite facts but cannot apply them.
entries.exAr: يرى المنتقدون أن *الحفظ الآلي* يُخرّج طلابًا يستطيعون ترديد الحقائق لكنهم لا يستطيعون تطبيقها.

entries.ex: Debating clubs help teenagers develop *critical thinking* and confidence.
entries.exAr: تساعد نوادي المناظرة المراهقين على تنمية *التفكير النقدي* والثقة بالنفس.

entries.ex: *Distance learning* allows people in remote areas to earn a degree from home.
entries.exAr: يتيح *التعلم عن بعد* لسكان المناطق النائية الحصول على شهادة جامعية من منازلهم.

entries.ex: Universities often look for applicants with strong *extracurricular* interests, such as volunteering.
entries.exAr: كثيرًا ما تبحث الجامعات عن متقدمين لديهم اهتمامات *لا صفية* قوية، مثل العمل التطوعي.

entries.ex: The *dropout* rate is highest among students who work long hours.
entries.exAr: يبلغ معدل *التسرب* من الدراسة أعلى مستوياته بين الطلاب الذين يعملون ساعات طويلة.

entries.ex: Many parents hire a private *tutor* to prepare their children for entrance exams.
entries.exAr: يستعين كثير من الآباء *بمدرّس خصوصي* لإعداد أبنائهم لامتحانات القبول.

entries.ex: She spent two years researching her *thesis* on water shortages in the region.
entries.exAr: أمضت عامين في البحث لإعداد *أطروحتها* حول شح المياه في المنطقة.

entries.ex: The *Faculty* of Medicine has opened a new research centre.
entries.exAr: افتتحت *كلية* الطب مركزًا بحثيًا جديدًا.

entries.ex: Strict *discipline* in the classroom does not always lead to better learning.
entries.exAr: لا يؤدي *الانضباط* الصارم في الفصل دائمًا إلى تعلم أفضل.

gap.s: Students who are caught committing ____ may be expelled from the university.
More than 2,000 students ____ on the new nursing degree last year.
Physical education is a ____ subject in all state primary schools.
Her excellent grades earned her a ____ to study medicine abroad.
The government plans to add climate science to the school ____.
Poor ____ is often the first sign that a student is having problems.
Not everyone wants a university degree; ____ training can also lead to well-paid jobs.
In one-to-one lessons, a good ____ can quickly identify a student's weaknesses.

para.a: Learning by memorising facts without understanding them is not effective.
para.b: *Rote learning* without real understanding is not effective.

para.a: People who leave school early often find it hard to get a job.
para.b: School *dropouts* frequently struggle to find employment.

para.a: Many young people now study online from home.
para.b: Many young people now study from home through *distance learning*.

para.a: Schools should teach students to question what they read.
para.b: Schools should foster *critical thinking* so that students evaluate what they read.

p1.q: Do you work or are you a student?
p1.a: I'm currently a final-year *undergraduate* studying civil engineering. It's quite demanding, especially now that I'm working on my final project, but I really enjoy it because the subject is very practical.

p1.q: What was your favourite subject at school?
p1.a: Definitely history. We had a brilliant teacher who never relied on *rote learning*; instead, she encouraged us to debate events and look at them from different angles, which made every lesson feel alive.

p1.q: Would you like to study online?
p1.a: Maybe for a short course, yes. *Distance learning* is flexible and saves time, but for a full degree I'd prefer a real campus, because I learn a lot from face-to-face discussions with classmates.

p2.cue: Describe a teacher who has influenced you.
points: what subject he or she taught
what this teacher did that was special
and explain why this teacher influenced you
p2.a: I'd like to talk about Mr Karim, who taught me maths in secondary school. Before I joined his class, I honestly thought I was hopeless with numbers, and my *numeracy* was quite weak for my age. What made him special was the way he taught. He rarely asked us to memorise formulas; instead, he showed us where they came from and how to use them in real situations, like working out a family budget. He also stayed after school twice a week to *tutor* anyone who was struggling, and he never made us feel embarrassed for asking questions. In a way, he was also a *mentor* to me. When I was choosing which *qualifications* to take, he helped me see that I could aim for engineering, which I had never considered. The reason he influenced me so much is that he changed my attitude. He taught me that ability grows with effort, and that lesson has stayed with me ever since. Without him, I don't think I'd be at university today.

p3.q: Should university education be free for everyone?
p3.a: I think it should be largely free, or at least heavily subsidised. High *tuition* fees discourage talented students from poorer families, and that is a waste of potential. However, a society also needs plumbers and electricians, so governments should invest just as much in *vocational* training, rather than pushing every young person towards a degree.

p3.q: How might technology change the way children learn in the future?
p3.a: I expect lessons to become much more personalised. Software can already track each child's progress and adjust the difficulty, so *assessment* could happen continuously rather than through one big exam. That said, I don't think technology will replace teachers, because children still need someone to inspire them, build *discipline* and help them develop social skills.

writing.q: Some people believe that schools should teach practical skills, such as managing money and cooking, rather than traditional academic subjects. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay: It is often argued that schools spend too much time on traditional *academic* subjects and too little on practical life skills such as managing money or cooking. While I accept that these skills are valuable, I disagree that they should replace subjects like mathematics, science and languages. In my view, a balanced *curriculum* can and should include both.

Admittedly, there are strong reasons to teach practical skills at school. Many young adults leave education without knowing how to plan a budget, understand a loan or prepare a healthy meal, and this can lead to debt and poor health later in life. Lessons in personal finance, for example, would build on basic *numeracy* and show *pupils* why mathematics matters in everyday situations. Such classes could also motivate students who find purely theoretical lessons difficult.

However, abandoning traditional subjects would be a serious mistake. Subjects such as history, literature and physics do far more than transmit facts; they develop *critical thinking*, careful reading and the ability to construct an argument, which are essential in almost every profession. Moreover, these subjects form the foundation of most university courses and professional *qualifications*, so a child who had not studied them would have far fewer options. Practical skills, by contrast, are relatively easy to learn later, either at home or through short courses.

In conclusion, although practical life skills deserve a place in schools, they should complement rather than replace academic subjects. The best approach is to integrate them into existing lessons and *extracurricular* activities, so that students leave school both knowledgeable and well prepared for adult life.
